newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Oil firms in Nigeria open overseas escrow accounts.
newsitem.headline: Oil firms in Nigeria open overseas escrow accounts.

text.p: Multinational oil companies in joint venture partnerships with Nigeria have now opened escrow accounts overseas to receive cash call payments as directed by the military government, company officials said on Friday.

"Government through its committee monitoring claims for cash calls gave the go-ahead last week for the affected oil companies to open escrow accounts with overseas banks," a spokesman for one of the companies involved said in Lagos.
Oil minister Dan Etete last year set up a committee to monitor claims for cash calls submitted by the multinationals.

He also ordered them to each open two escrow accounts -- in Lagos and overseas -- to be supervised by the Central Bank for cash call payments through state oil company NNPC, which would also monitor how the money was being spent.
Cash calls are NNPC's payments for any joint projects.
The six multinationals in joint ventures with Nigeria are Royal Dutch/Shell, Mobil Corp, Texaco Inc, Chevron Corp, Elf Aquitaine and Agip SpA.
The companies collectively produce Nigeria's nearly two million barrels of crude daily, accounting for slightly more than 90 percent of its foreign exchange earnings.
The multinationals have been complaining about government's delay in paying the cash calls and industry sources say the arrears owed by Nigeria currently stand at $1.5 billion.

NNPC officials said the delay was caused by inability of the Etete committee to effectively relate with the joint venture partners, who had resisted opening escrow accounts which would be under the constant scrutiny of the committee.

An official of one of the multinationals said there would be duplication in the system, adding: "The oil companies are required to submit cash calls claims to NNPC as well as to the Etete committee, slowing work in the process."
